source.title: A Rationale from a Frequency Perspective for Grokking in Training Neural Networks
source.authors: Zhang-Chen Zhou; Yaoyu Zhang; Zhi-Qin John Xu

record.tranche_reason: The study empirically tests grokking and its training dynamics using frequency-spectrum measurements, rather than reproducing the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own parity, frequency-dynamics, and MNIST results. Findings cited from other work are excluded. Several reported values are available only in figures.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own experiments on (10,[10]) parity, 1D synthetic regression and MNIST. It reports when delayed generalization appears, how the delay shifts with training-set proportion, and how initialization scale switches it on or off. It uses a frequency-spectrum method rather than the original setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors argue that nonuniform or insufficient sampling puts spurious frequencies in the training data. Networks fit these first: low frequencies under the F-Principle with default init, or all frequencies at a similar pace with large init. This yields grokking without explicit regularization or a lazy-to-rich transition. The account is empirical only, and they say it may not apply to language-based grokking, which includes the algorithmic datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses frequency-spectrum analysis on synthetic regression, parity, and MNIST tasks, rather than reproducing the original grokking experiments or their measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes differ with training-data proportion and sampling distribution, and with MNIST initialization setting. The MNIST initialization comparison also changes the optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: During delayed generalization, output spectra first fit spurious low-frequency components (aliasing from undersampling). These decay as high frequencies are learned, on parity (Fig. 5) and synthetic data (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking-like delays arise when training-set spectra contain spurious frequencies that the network's frequency bias fits first.

record.problems: The study describes the mechanism as empirical and supplies no comprehensive theory. Several key curves are figure-only. In the MNIST comparison, initialization and optimizer both change, confounding attribution to initialization.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the tested versions were left out.

untested.parts: No test-accuracy curve showing a chance-level plateau then a jump; error curves are figure-only (Fig. 17). No numeric delays. Parity is the only algorithmic task; no modular arithmetic.
No circuit identification, no removal of memorizing components, and no progress measure shown to anticipate the jump.
No text or molecule data, no weight-norm manipulation, no lazy-to-rich analysis. Initialization effect is not isolated from the optimizer.
No weight decay, efficiency account, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.
No optimizer or floating-point artifact tests.

missing.what: 1D synthetic sin 6x loss curves: grokking with 65 nonuniform points, absent with 1000 nonuniform and with 65 uniform points (sin activation, 10 trials).
Same synthetic grokking replicated with ReLU and tanh activations; absent at n=1000.
Parity test-error curves for all proportions and for the 0.5 run, needed to read the accuracy jump.

record.verdict_notes: Most evidence is figure-only, with no numeric delays or accuracies. The authors' caveat that the mechanism may not cover algorithmic datasets limits how far the parity V1 result generalizes. The MNIST α comparison confounds initialization with optimizer (Adam vs SGD) and learning rate. I treat this as weakening the V3 support rather than as a scope limit. The text supplied is the arXiv v1 preprint; the DOI points to the published CiCP version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not state a chance-level test-accuracy phase for each training-set proportion, or report a numeric optimization-delay comparison.
The study measures frequency components, not an identified generalizing circuit; it does not establish removal of a memorizing circuit or analyze modular addition.
Tests MNIST and initialization scale, but not text, molecules, weight norm, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Does not test an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not compare identified algorithms across runs.
Does not test optimizer or numerical-precision artifact explanations.

rows.subject: width-1000 two-layer fully-connected NN
rows.operation_detail: Track frequency spectra during parity-function training.
rows.baseline: training-set spectrum has spurious low-frequency components relative to the full-data spectrum
rows.value: The network first fits spurious low-frequency components; as it learns high-frequency components, the low-frequency components decrease toward the true spectrum.
rows.note: The authors describe this progression as preceding improved generalization; the measurements are frequency spectra, not identified circuits.
rows.check: Output frequency spectra are a function-space measure, not an identified generalizing or memorizing circuit. No timing shows the spectra anticipate the jump. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: four-hidden-layer fully-connected NN
rows.operation_detail: Track output frequency spectra during training on the synthetic sin 6x dataset.
rows.value: The low-frequency components initially deviate substantially from the target and decrease as training proceeds; the training-set low-frequency amplitude remains unchanged.
rows.note: The paper attributes the later change to learning high-frequency components and frequency aliasing.
rows.check: Synthetic sin 6x regression spectrum is not a circuit or progress measure on an algorithmic task. Move to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: 1D synthetic sin 6x regression, default initialization (text-based; no rows)
relationships.reason: From the text (Fig. 1): with default init, the delay appears for 65 nonuniform points but vanishes for 65 uniform or 1000 points. So sampling distribution, not just the training regime, switches it.
relationships.display_finding: The delay appeared with 65 nonuniform samples but vanished with 65 uniform samples or 1000 samples under default initialization.
